Stillvaro 2.0 — Memorize the digits of π. Four digits at a time.

article.p: Open this guide in Your memory → What the numbers mean or Settings → Help → What the numbers mean. Numbers describe saved practice, not intelligence or a guarantee of future recall.

Digit 1 is π’s leading 3. A group has four digits. Learning trends and anchor sections hold up to five groups (20 digits); practice passages connect up to four groups (16 digits), including overlapping joins and shorter repairs.

tr.td: Completed groups continuously from π. Current acquisition requires three clean recalls; later groups also need two successful incoming joins. Watching or opening the next group is not completion.
The longest exact passage from π recalled without help in connected practice. Separate successes are not added together.
Whole groups before the first mistake in saved manual tests or qualifying older scheduled full cold checks from π. Anchor tests do not increase this record.

article.p: The opening 3141 advances after one guided entry; later practice supplies its recall evidence. Completed prefix credit and saved achievements do not fade on a timer. Current connected passages can leave Recalled together at sixteen while practice continues farther; a memory test can measure longer recall. Older passages can preserve larger achievements.
Origin insights follow the contiguous practiced area and its next available group. Browsing ahead and practice from another start do not fill gaps in that path.
All three visuals follow the selected section.

tr.td: Blue solid line/circles: Unaided. Amber dashed line/squares: Help. Both use 0–100%.
Up to 32 measured snapshots per series, placed at their actual dates. Touch to inspect a snapshot, percentage, and attempt count. Not daily averages.
One row per four digits. Unaided and Help colors strengthen as percentages increase.
Current retained outcomes for each group; the attempt count accompanies the row. — means no measured value, not failure.
Rows identify groups; columns are their 1st–4th positions. Numbers count wrong taps; stronger color means more within the selected section.
Retained practice errors with a valid digit position and attempted digit. Hints are excluded. Unpositioned errors are counted below the map.

article.p: The chart shows earlier snapshots; the group heatmap shows current data. Empty or older snapshots without attempt counts are omitted. A single snapshot appears as points without an invented history. Series use both color and shape; heatmaps print values, and VoiceOver reads each cell’s group or digit.

tr.td: Successful unaided outcomes ÷ eligible outcomes from ordinary practice, isolated probes, and older practice checks.
Guided completions remain in the denominator. Possible answer-search attempts and older outcomes without recall evidence are excluded. Repeating a group adds attempts. Manual tests stay separate.
For an eligible successful attempt: 80% previous estimate + 20% answer information supplied.
No answers supplied = 0%; all four supplied = 100%. New groups start at 100% while unknown. Section snapshots average groups equally, including new groups; unmeasured heatmap rows show a dash.

article.p: Unaided recall and help are not complementary percentages. Help is a smoothed estimate of information supplied, not an error rate. Successful isolated checks contribute zero help; possible answer-search attempts do not update the estimate.

Slip counts describe events, not failed groups, unique digits, or lifetime totals. One attempt can add several wrong taps. Manual Memory Test misses appear in test results instead. Undo does not remove previously saved mistakes or help. Trying three distinct wrong digits at one position can flag possible answer search; a typo or slow answer alone does not establish it. Older flags may retain earlier rules.

tr.td: Complete groups of four before the first wrong group. A correct retry cannot restart the score. An unfinished group adds nothing.
Submitted groups counted once, including misses. Retries add no extra digits.
Best saved manual test from the same starting group. Twelve digits from digit 21 means twelve from that anchor, not thirty-two from π.
Groups missed, even if a later retry succeeds. The range identifies the group, not an exact wrong digit.

article.p: Tests check the whole group on its fourth digit. They use Memory only, four attempts per group, no skipping, and no timer. A correct answer advances; four misses or Finish end and save the test. Undo before submission uses no attempt and refunds none. Tests preserve lessons, input, and review schedules.
Memory checks plots up to 24 recent self-tests from π. Anchor tests and older scheduled checks appear separately. Earlier results may retain different scoring precision or skipped groups.

tr.td: A repair or frozen state takes priority over past success.
A passage review containing the group is due.
No connected recall for the incoming join; the opening group is recorded from π.
Connected recall on at least three distinct local dates in the current evidence set.
Connected recall with fewer than three qualifying dates.

article.p: The first group of a later passage is an entry cue; alone it cannot establish its incoming join. Misses or help can reset the date set. Category colors are separate from the orb’s digit colors and are not retention percentages.

Reviews follow exact passages. Successful recall can schedule one day, then six, then longer intervals. Help or a miss brings the passage back sooner. Early success usually leaves the date unchanged, except for the next success after a reset. A longer successful passage can replace shorter reviews inside it; overlaps may remain separate. Dates suggest when to return, not how much you will remember.

Most diagnostic and metric lists retain up to 256 recent entries; recent answer-search flags retain ten per group. Test records are separate. Rounded percentages can change as old observations leave these lists. Erase all progress and settings clears local records; device backups are managed separately.

Older summaries may show Studied, Strong now, Still forming, and Ready to revisit as counts of four-digit groups. Their bar is a distribution, not a timeline; an older Digits recalled total can include groups recalled separately.

Older diagnostic fields remain in saved data: recovery compares successful resumptions with opportunities after a miss; anchor-entry rate uses first-group outcomes from earlier scheduled cold checks, excluding manual anchor tests. These are not displayed in the simplified Learning trends view. Error classifications and recent search flags also remain recorded.

div.p: A little practice. A different way to see π.
